verses.text: Jesus and his followers went across the lake to the area of the Gadarenes.
When Jesus got out of the boat, a man with an evil spirit came out from the tombs straight away to meet him.
This man lived among the tombs. No one could keep him tied up any more, not even with a chain.
People had often tied his hands and feet with chains, but he tore the chains apart and broke the irons on his feet. No one was strong enough to control him.
All night and all day he stayed among the tombs and in the hills. He kept screaming and cutting himself with stones.
When he saw Jesus far away, he ran and fell on his knees in front of him.
He shouted with a loud voice, "What do you want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? In God's name, I beg you, do not hurt me!"
He said this because Jesus had said to him, "Come out of this man, you evil spirit!"
Then Jesus asked him, "What is your name?" "My name is Legion," he answered, "because there are many of us."
And he begged Jesus again and again not to send them out of that area.
A large herd of pigs was feeding on the nearby hillside.
The demons begged Jesus, "Send us among the pigs. Let us go into them."
Jesus let them do it. The evil spirits came out of the man and went into the pigs. There were about two thousand pigs in the herd. The whole herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and drowned.
The men looking after the pigs ran off. They told the news in the town and in the countryside. The people went out to see what had happened.
They came to Jesus and saw the man who had been controlled by the many demons. He was sitting there, wearing clothes and thinking clearly. And the people were afraid.
Those who had seen it told the people what had happened to the man with the demons, and about the pigs.
Then the people began to beg Jesus to leave their area.
As Jesus was getting into the boat, the man who had had the demons begged to go with him.
But Jesus did not let him. He said, "Go home to your family and friends. Tell them how much the Lord has done for you, and how he has been kind to you."
So the man went away and began to tell people in the Ten Towns how much Jesus had done for him. And all the people were amazed.
Jesus crossed over by boat to the other side of the lake again. A large crowd gathered around him while he was by the lake.
Then a man named Jairus came there. He was one of the leaders of the synagogue. When he saw Jesus, he fell at his feet.
He begged Jesus again and again, "My little daughter is dying. Please come and put your hands on her so that she will be healed and live."
So Jesus went with him. A large crowd followed and pushed against him from every side.
A woman was there who had been bleeding for twelve years.
She had suffered a great deal, even though many doctors had treated her. She had spent all the money she had, but she was getting worse instead of better.
She had heard about Jesus. So she came up behind him in the crowd and touched his clothes.
She thought, "If I just touch his clothes, I will be healed."
Straight away her bleeding stopped. She felt in her body that she was free from her suffering.
At once Jesus knew that power had gone out from him. He turned around in the crowd and asked, "Who touched my clothes?"
His followers answered, "You see how the people are crowding against you. So how can you ask, 'Who touched me?'"
But Jesus kept looking around to see who had done it.
Then the woman came and fell at his feet. She was shaking with fear, because she knew what had happened to her. She told him the whole truth.
He said to her, "Daughter, your faith has healed you. Go in peace. You are free from your suffering."
While Jesus was still speaking, some men came from the house of Jairus, the synagogue leader. "Your daughter is dead," they said. "Why bother the Teacher any more?"
Jesus heard what they said. He told the synagogue leader, "Do not be afraid. Just believe."
He did not let anyone follow him except Peter, James and John, the brother of James.
They came to the home of the synagogue leader. There Jesus saw a lot of noise and confusion. People were crying and wailing loudly.
He went inside and said to them, "Why all this noise and crying? The child is not dead. She is only sleeping."
But they laughed at him. He sent them all outside. Then he took the child's father and mother and the followers who were with him, and he went in where the child was.
He took her by the hand and said to her, "Talitha koum!" This means, "Little girl, I tell you, get up!"
Straight away the girl stood up and began to walk around. She was twelve years old. When this happened, everyone was completely amazed.
Jesus gave strict orders not to let anyone know about this. And he told them to give her something to eat.
